    (hX : Exchangeable μ X) (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) : Contractable μ X :=

docstring: Contractability is equivalent to invariance of the path law under every strictly increasing time-reindexing `ℕ → ℕ`. This is the path-law form of spreadability/contractability.
code:
theorem contractable_iff_forall_map_reindex_pathLaw {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) :
    Contractable μ X ↔
      ∀ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ →
        (pathLaw μ X).map (fun x : ℕ → α => fun k => x (φ k)) = pathLaw μ X := by

docstring: Contractability is equivalent to preservation of the path law by every strictly increasing time-reindexing `ℕ → ℕ`.
code:
theorem contractable_iff_forall_measurePreserving_reindex {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) :
    Contractable μ X ↔
      ∀ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ →
        MeasurePreserving (fun x : ℕ → α => fun k => x (φ k)) (pathLaw μ X) (pathLaw μ X) := by

docstring: **Every exchangeable sequence with a.e. measurable coordinates is contractable**: along any strictly increasing finite selection `k`, `blockLaw μ X k = prefixLaw μ X m`. One direction of the de Finetti–Ryll-Nardzewski equivalence.
code:
theorem contractable_of_exchangeable {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    (hX : Exchangeable μ X) (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) : Contractable μ X :=

docstring: The block cylinder event on the selected coordinates: `{ω | ∀ i, X (k i) ω ∈ C i}`.
code: def blockCylinder (X : ℕ → Ω → α) {m : ℕ} (k : Fin m → ℕ) (C : Fin m → Set α) : Set Ω :=

docstring: The block cylinder is the preimage of the rectangle `Set.univ.pi C` under the selected-coordinate map `ω ↦ (X (k ·) ω)`.
code:
theorem blockCylinder_eq_preimage_univ_pi (X : ℕ → Ω → α) {m : ℕ} (k : Fin m → ℕ)
    (C : Fin m → Set α) :
    blockCylinder X k C = (fun ω i => X (k i) ω) ⁻¹' Set.univ.pi C := by

docstring: The product of the selected coordinate indicators, `∏ i, 𝟙_{C i}(X (k i) ω)`.
code: def blockIndicatorProd (X : ℕ → Ω → α) {m : ℕ} (k : Fin m → ℕ) (C : Fin m → Set α) : Ω → ℝ :=

docstring: Pointwise value of the indicator product: the product of the selected coordinate indicators.
code:
theorem blockIndicatorProd_apply (X : ℕ → Ω → α) {m : ℕ} (k : Fin m → ℕ) (C : Fin m → Set α)
    (ω : Ω) :
    blockIndicatorProd X k C ω = ∏ i, (C i).indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) (X (k i) ω) := by

docstring: The empty (zero-coordinate) indicator product is the constant-one function.
code:
theorem blockIndicatorProd_empty (X : ℕ → Ω → α) (k : Fin 0 → ℕ) (C : Fin 0 → Set α) :
    blockIndicatorProd X k C = fun _ => 1 := by

docstring: The indicator product is the indicator of the block cylinder.
code:
theorem blockIndicatorProd_eq_indicator (X : ℕ → Ω → α) {m : ℕ} (k : Fin m → ℕ)
    (C : Fin m → Set α) :
    blockIndicatorProd X k C = (blockCylinder X k C).indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) := by

docstring: **Successor split of the indicator product.** Splitting off the last selected coordinate, the length-`r+1` indicator product equals the indicator of the length-`r` prefix cylinder intersected with the last coordinate's preimage. The `Fin 0` companion is `blockIndicatorProd_empty`.
code:
theorem blockIndicatorProd_succ_eq_indicator_inter (X : ℕ → Ω → α) {r : ℕ} (k : Fin (r + 1) → ℕ)
    (C : Fin (r + 1) → Set α) :
    blockIndicatorProd X k C
      = (blockCylinder X (fun i : Fin r => k i.castSucc) (fun j => C j.castSucc)
          ∩ X (k (Fin.last r)) ⁻¹' C (Fin.last r)).indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) := by

docstring: The block law evaluated on a measurable rectangle is the measure of the block cylinder: `blockLaw μ X k (Set.univ.pi C) = μ (blockCylinder X k C)`. A `blockCylinder`-named restatement of the merged `blockLaw_apply_rectangle`.
The indicator product is integrable under a finite measure (a.e.-measurable coordinates).

The real (Bochner) integral of the indicator product is the block law of the rectangle: `∫ ω, ∏ i, 𝟙_{C i}(X (k i) ω) ∂μ = (blockLaw μ X k (∏ᵢ C i)).toReal` — the real (`toReal`) form of the `ℝ≥0∞` identity `lintegral_blockCylinder_indicator` (integrability under a finite measure is `integrable_blockIndicatorProd`).
code:
theorem integral_blockIndicatorProd {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α} {m : ℕ}
    {k : Fin m → ℕ} {C : Fin m → Set α} (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X (k i)) μ)
    (hC : ∀ i, MeasurableSet (C i)) :
    ∫ ω, blockIndicatorProd X k C ω ∂μ = (blockLaw μ X k (Set.univ.pi C)).toReal := by

docstring: **The block law of a rectangle is the lintegral of the block-cylinder indicator.** For a.e.-measurable selected coordinates, `∫⁻ ω, 𝟙_{blockCylinder X k C}(ω) ∂μ = blockLaw μ X k (∏ᵢ C i)`. Being an `ℝ≥0∞` lintegral, this is the honest identity for an **arbitrary** measure (no finiteness needed).
code:
theorem lintegral_blockCylinder_indicator {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α} {m : ℕ}
    {k : Fin m → ℕ} {C : Fin m → Set α} (hX : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X (k i)) μ)
    (hC : ∀ i, MeasurableSet (C i)) :
    ∫⁻ ω, (blockCylinder X k C).indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ≥0∞)) ω ∂μ
      = blockLaw μ X k (Set.univ.pi C) := by

docstring: The block cylinder of a process with measurable selected coordinates on measurable sets is measurable.
Membership in the block cylinder: `ω` lies in `blockCylinder X k C` iff every selected coordinate `X (k i) ω` lies in its set `C i`.
code:
theorem mem_blockCylinder {X : ℕ → Ω → α} {m : ℕ} {k : Fin m → ℕ} {C : Fin m → Set α} {ω : Ω} :
    ω ∈ blockCylinder X k C ↔ ∀ i, X (k i) ω ∈ C i :=

docstring: **The covariance of two disjoint block averages of a contractable L² sequence.** Two block averages over selections `k : Fin n → ℕ` and `k' : Fin m → ℕ` with disjoint ranges (`0 < n`, `0 < m`) have covariance exactly the common off-diagonal covariance `c = cov[X 0, X 1]`, regardless of the two block lengths.
code:
theorem Contractable.covariance_blockAverage_of_disjoint [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hX : Contractable μ X)
    (hX_L2 : ∀ n, MemLp (X n) 2 μ) {n m : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hm : 0 < m) {k : Fin n → ℕ}
    {k' : Fin m → ℕ} (hdisj : ∀ i j, k i ≠ k' j) :
    cov[blockAverage X k, blockAverage X k'; μ] = cov[X 0, X 1; μ] := by

docstring: **The mean of a block average of a contractable process.** A block average over any selection of length `0 < n` has the common coordinate mean `μ[X 0]`.
code:
theorem Contractable.integral_blockAverage (hX : Contractable μ X)
    (hint0 : Integrable (X 0) μ) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {k : Fin n → ℕ}
    (hint : ∀ i, Integrable (X (k i)) μ) :
    μ[blockAverage X k] = μ[X 0] := by

docstring: **The two-window L² distance for block averages.** Since two disjoint block averages of a contractable process share the common mean `μ[X 0]`, the two-window variance bound is the squared `L²` distance between them: ```text ∫ (blockAverage X k - blockAverage X k')² dμ = (v - c) / n + (v - c) / m. ```
code:
theorem Contractable.integral_sq_blockAverage_sub_of_disjoint [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    (hX : Contractable μ X) (hX_L2 : ∀ n, MemLp (X n) 2 μ) {n m : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hm : 0 < m)
    {k : Fin n → ℕ} {k' : Fin m → ℕ}
    (hk : Function.Injective k) (hk' : Function.Injective k') (hdisj : ∀ i j, k i ≠ k' j) :
    ∫ ω, (blockAverage X k ω - blockAverage X k' ω) ^ 2 ∂μ
      = (Var[X 0; μ] - cov[X 0, X 1; μ]) / n + (Var[X 0; μ] - cov[X 0, X 1; μ]) / m := by

docstring: **The variance of a block average of a contractable L² sequence.** For a contractable real-valued process with `L²` coordinates and an injective selection `k : Fin n → ℕ` (`0 < n`), the block average has the closed-form variance `(v - c) / n + c`, where `v = Var[X 0]` is the common coordinate variance and `c = cov[X 0, X 1]` is the common off-diagonal covariance.
code:
theorem Contractable.variance_blockAverage [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hX : Contractable μ X)
    (hX_L2 : ∀ n, MemLp (X n) 2 μ) {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {k : Fin n → ℕ}
    (hk : Function.Injective k) :
    Var[blockAverage X k; μ] = (Var[X 0; μ] - cov[X 0, X 1; μ]) / n + cov[X 0, X 1; μ] := by

docstring: **The two-window L² bound for block averages.** For a contractable real-valued process with `L²` coordinates, two block averages over injective selections `k : Fin n → ℕ` and `k' : Fin m → ℕ` with disjoint ranges (`0 < n`, `0 < m`) satisfy ```text Var[blockAverage X k - blockAverage X k'] = (v - c) / n + (v - c) / m, ``` where `v = Var[X 0]` and `c = cov[X 0, X 1]`. The bound vanishes as the block lengths grow, which is the analytic core of the L² route to de Finetti's theorem.
code:
theorem Contractable.variance_blockAverage_sub_of_disjoint [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    (hX : Contractable μ X) (hX_L2 : ∀ n, MemLp (X n) 2 μ) {n m : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hm : 0 < m)
    {k : Fin n → ℕ} {k' : Fin m → ℕ}
    (hk : Function.Injective k) (hk' : Function.Injective k') (hdisj : ∀ i j, k i ≠ k' j) :
    Var[blockAverage X k - blockAverage X k'; μ]
      = (Var[X 0; μ] - cov[X 0, X 1; μ]) / n + (Var[X 0; μ] - cov[X 0, X 1; μ]) / m := by

docstring: The **block average** of a real-valued process `X` over a finite selection `k : Fin n → ℕ`: the empirical mean `n⁻¹ • ∑ i, X (k i)` of the block `(X (k i))ᵢ`.
code: def blockAverage (X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ) {n : ℕ} (k : Fin n → ℕ) : Ω → ℝ :=

theorem blockAverage_apply {n : ℕ} (k : Fin n → ℕ) (ω : Ω) :
    blockAverage X k ω = (n : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i, X (k i) ω := by

docstring: A block average as a real-scaled finite sum.

    MemLp (blockAverage X k) 2 μ := by

docstring: The double sum of block covariances splits along the diagonal into the common variance and the common off-diagonal covariance of a contractable `L²` sequence.
code:
private theorem sum_sum_cov_eq (hX : Contractable μ X)
    (hmeas : ∀ m, AEMeasurable (X m) μ) {n : ℕ} {k : Fin n → ℕ} (hk : Function.Injective k) :
    ∑ i, ∑ j, cov[X (k i), X (k j); μ]
      = (n : ℝ) ^ 2 * cov[X 0, X 1; μ] + n * (Var[X 0; μ] - cov[X 0, X 1; μ]) := by

docstring: A measurable real-valued observable with square-integrable coordinates, applied coordinatewise to a contractable process, gives uniform means, variances, and off-diagonal covariances: the means agree across all coordinates, so do the variances, and every covariance of two distinct coordinates takes the same value.
code:
theorem Contractable.covariance_structure_comp {μ : Measure Ω} {X : ℕ → Ω → α}
    (hX_contractable : Contractable μ X) (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ) {f : α → ℝ}
    (hf : Measurable f) (hL2 : ∀ i, MemLp (fun ω => f (X i ω)) 2 μ) :
    (∀ i j, μ[fun ω => f (X i ω)] = μ[fun ω => f (X j ω)]) ∧
      (∀ i j, Var[fun ω => f (X i ω); μ] = Var[fun ω => f (X j ω); μ]) ∧
      (∀ i j k l, i ≠ j → k ≠ l →
        cov[fun ω => f (X i ω), fun ω => f (X j ω); μ] =
          cov[fun ω => f (X k ω), fun ω => f (X l ω); μ]) :=

docstring: A bounded measurable real-valued observable of a contractable process has uniform means, variances, and off-diagonal covariances. On a finite measure space the square-integrability of the mapped coordinates is automatic, so only an a.e. bound on each coordinate is required.
code:
theorem Contractable.covariance_structure_comp_of_bound {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    {X : ℕ → Ω → α} (hX_contractable : Contractable μ X) (hX_meas : ∀ i, AEMeasurable (X i) μ)
    {f : α → ℝ} (hf : Measurable f) (C : ℝ) (hf_bound : ∀ i, ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, |f (X i ω)| ≤ C) :
    (∀ i j, μ[fun ω => f (X i ω)] = μ[fun ω => f (X j ω)]) ∧
      (∀ i j, Var[fun ω => f (X i ω); μ] = Var[fun ω => f (X j ω); μ]) ∧
      (∀ i j k l, i ≠ j → k ≠ l →
        cov[fun ω => f (X i ω), fun ω => f (X j ω); μ] =
          cov[fun ω => f (X k ω), fun ω => f (X l ω); μ]) :=

docstring: **Uniform covariances from contractability.** For a contractable real-valued process with a.e. measurable coordinates, any two off-diagonal covariances agree: `cov[X i, X j; μ] = cov[X k, X l; μ]` whenever `i < j` and `k < l`.

    (hij : i < j) (hkl : k < l) :
    cov[X i, X j; μ] = cov[X k, X l; μ] := by

docstring: **Uniform off-diagonal covariances from contractability.** For a contractable real-valued process with a.e. measurable coordinates, any two off-diagonal covariances agree: `cov[X i, X j; μ] = cov[X k, X l; μ]` whenever `i ≠ j` and `k ≠ l`.

docstring: **The uniform covariance structure of a contractable L² sequence.** A contractable real-valued process with `L²` coordinates has constant coordinate means and variances, and a single common off-diagonal covariance: any two unequal-index pairs have equal covariance. This is the seed of the Layer 3 L² route to de Finetti.
code:
theorem contractable_covariance_structure (hX : Contractable μ X) (hX_L2 : ∀ n, MemLp (X n) 2 μ) :
    (∀ i j, μ[X i] = μ[X j]) ∧ (∀ i j, Var[X i; μ] = Var[X j; μ]) ∧
      (∀ i j k l, i ≠ j → k ≠ l → cov[X i, X j; μ] = cov[X k, X l; μ]) := by

docstring: **The exact long-average versus tail-average `L²` bound.** For a contractable process, the squared `L²` distance between the average of the first `n` coordinates and the average of the following `n` coordinates is `2 * (v - c) / n`.

    ∫ ω, (prefixAverage X n ω - followingAverage X n ω) ^ 2 ∂μ =
      2 * (Var[X 0; μ] - cov[X 0, X 1; μ]) / n := by

docstring: The long-average versus tail-average squared `L²` distance tends to zero. The use of blocks of length `n + 1` avoids a separate convention for the empty average.

      atTop (𝓝 0) := by

docstring: **Identification of the reverse-martingale limit.** If `μ[f | 𝔽 n]` converges to `Xlim` both almost everywhere and in `L¹`, along an antitone filtration, then `Xlim` is the conditional expectation of `f` on the tail σ-algebra `⨅ n, 𝔽 n`. The proof uses the a.e. convergence to make `Xlim` measurable for `⨅ n, 𝔽 n`, and the `L¹` convergence to transport the tower property `μ[μ[f | 𝔽 n] | ⨅ n, 𝔽 n] =ᵐ μ[f | ⨅ n, 𝔽 n]` to the limit.

      Tendsto (fun n => eLpNorm (μ[f | 𝔽 n] - μ[f | ⨅ n, 𝔽 n]) 1 μ) atTop (𝓝 0) := by

docstring: **Time-reversal crossing bound.** For a process `X` with `k` upcrossings `[a→b]` completing before time `N`, the time-reversed negated process `-(revProcess X N)` has its `k`-th upcrossing `[-b→-a]` completing at time `≤ N`.

docstring: Strong version tracking the bijection explicitly. For `m ≤ k` with `X`'s `k`-th crossing completing before `N`: `upperCrossingTime Y (N + 1) m ≤ N - lowerCrossingTime X (k - m)`.     (hm : m ≤ k)
    (h_k : upperCrossingTime a b X N k ω < N) :
    upperCrossingTime (-b) (-a) (-(revProcess X N)) (N + 1) m ω
      ≤ N - lowerCrossingTime a b X N (k - m) ω := by

docstring: Inductive step of `upperCrossingTime_neg_revProcess_le_strong`. Fix a crossing index `i` and a count `m'`, and assume: * `hab : a < b`; * `hσ_lt_N`: `X`'s `(i + 1)`-th upper crossing completes strictly before `N`; * `ih'`: the reversed process satisfies the bound at count `m'` (endpoint index `i + 1`).     (hσ_lt_N : upperCrossingTime a b X N (i + 1) ω < N)
    (ih' : upperCrossingTime (-b) (-a) (-(revProcess X N)) (N + 1) m' ω

    upperCrossingTime (-b) (-a) (-(revProcess X N)) (N + 1) (m' + 1) ω

**Lévy's downward theorem specializes correctly to an eventually constant filtration.** Run the flagship `MeasureTheory.tendsto_ae_condExp_iInf` on an antitone filtration that is constant from index `N` on, then collapse its limit through `condExp_iInf_eq_of_eventually_const`. docstring: **Moment determinacy, exponential-moment form (the roadmap's B1 hypothesis).** A finite measure on `ℝ` for which some exponential moment `∫ e^{a|x|} dμ` with `a > 0` is finite is determined by its polynomial moments. docstring: Products preserve the ambient-isotopy relation: if `f` and `f'` are ambient isotopic in `Y` and `g` and `g'` are ambient isotopic in `Y'`, then `f.prodMap g` and `f'.prodMap g'` are ambient isotopic in `Y × Y'`, via the product ambient isotopy.
code:
theorem prodMap (h : AmbientIsotopic f f') (h' : AmbientIsotopic g g') :
    AmbientIsotopic (f.prodMap g) (f'.prodMap g') := by

docstring: The final map of a product ambient isotopy is the product of the two final maps.
code:
theorem final_prodCongr (Φ : AmbientIsotopy Y) (Ψ : AmbientIsotopy Y') (y : Y × Y') :
    (Φ.prodCongr Ψ).final y = (Φ.final y.1, Ψ.final y.2) := rfl

docstring: The **product of two ambient isotopies**, sharing the time parameter: from an ambient isotopy `Φ` of `Y` and one `Ψ` of `Y'` build an ambient isotopy of `Y × Y'` whose value at `(t, (y, y'))` is `(Φ (t, y), Ψ (t, y'))`. Its total map is a homeomorphism, being an embedding (by `isEmbedding_mergeTotal`) and surjective (each factor is surjective at every time, by `AmbientIsotopy.isHomeomorph_apply`).
code: def prodCongr (Φ : AmbientIsotopy Y) (Ψ : AmbientIsotopy Y') : AmbientIsotopy (Y × Y') where

theorem prodCongr_apply (Φ : AmbientIsotopy Y) (Ψ : AmbientIsotopy Y') (p : I × (Y × Y')) :
    (Φ.prodCongr Ψ).toContinuousMap p =
      (Φ.toContinuousMap (p.1, p.2.1), Ψ.toContinuousMap (p.1, p.2.2)) := rfl

docstring: Products preserve the isotopy relation: if `f₀ ≈ f₁` and `g₀ ≈ g₁`, then `f₀.prodMap g₀ ≈ f₁.prodMap g₁`.
code:
theorem prodMap (h : Isotopic f₀ f₁) (h' : Isotopic g₀ g₁) :
    Isotopic (f₀.prodMap g₀) (f₁.prodMap g₁) :=

docstring: The **product of two isotopies**, sharing the time parameter: from an isotopy `f₀ ≈ f₁` and an isotopy `g₀ ≈ g₁` build an isotopy `f₀.prodMap g₀ ≈ f₁.prodMap g₁` whose value at `(t, (x, x'))` is `(F (t, x), G (t, x'))`. The underlying homotopy is Mathlib's `ContinuousMap.Homotopy.prodMap`; the total map is an embedding by `isEmbedding_mergeTotal`.
code:
@[expose] def prodMap (F : Isotopy f₀ f₁) (G : Isotopy g₀ g₁) :
    Isotopy (f₀.prodMap g₀) (f₁.prodMap g₁) where

theorem prodMap_apply (F : Isotopy f₀ f₁) (G : Isotopy g₀ g₁) (p : I × (X × X')) :
    F.prodMap G p = (F (p.1, p.2.1), G (p.1, p.2.2)) := rfl

docstring: The time-duplicating map `(t, (x, x')) ↦ ((t, x), (t, x'))` is a topological embedding: it has the continuous left inverse `((a, x), (b, x')) ↦ (a, (x, x'))`.
code:
private theorem isEmbedding_dupTime :
    IsEmbedding fun p : I × (X × X') => ((p.1, p.2.1), (p.1, p.2.2)) := by

docstring: The core embedding lemma shared by the isotopy and ambient-isotopy products. If `u` and `v` are embeddings of `I × X → I × Y` and `I × X' → I × Y'` that preserve the time coordinate, then the *merged* total map `(t, (x, x')) ↦ (t, ((u (t, x)).2, (v (t, x')).2))` reading both at the same time `t` is an embedding. It factors as the time-duplicating embedding, then `u × v`, then the projection identifying the two (equal) time coordinates.
code:
theorem isEmbedding_mergeTotal {u : C(I × X, I × Y)} {v : C(I × X', I × Y')}
    (hu : IsEmbedding u) (hv : IsEmbedding v) (hu1 : ∀ p, (u p).1 = p.1)
    (hv1 : ∀ p, (v p).1 = p.1) :
    IsEmbedding fun p : I × (X × X') => (p.1, ((u (p.1, p.2.1)).2, (v (p.1, p.2.2)).2)) := by

docstring: If `trans γ (symm γ') = refl`, then `γ = γ'`. This is the quotient analogue of `eq_of_div_eq_one : a / b = 1 → a = b`.
code:
theorem eq_of_trans_symm {γ γ' : Homotopic.Quotient x₀ x₁}
    (h : trans γ (symm γ') = refl x₀) : γ = γ' := by

docstring: The quotient topology on path-homotopy classes. This instance is load-bearing: `Path.Homotopic.Quotient` is a `def` over `Quotient`, and instance search does not unfold it to find the generic `TopologicalSpace (Quotient _)`.

instance instTopologicalSpace (x₀ x : X) :
    TopologicalSpace (Path.Homotopic.Quotient x₀ x) :=

docstring: A set of path-homotopy classes is open exactly when its preimage under quotient construction is open.
code:
theorem isOpen_iff_preimage_mk {x₀ x₁ : X} {S : Set (Path.Homotopic.Quotient x₀ x₁)} :
    IsOpen S ↔ IsOpen ((Path.Homotopic.Quotient.mk : Path x₀ x₁ →
      Path.Homotopic.Quotient x₀ x₁) ⁻¹' S) :=

docstring: Casting the reflexivity class at `x` along `h : y = x` gives the reflexivity class at `y`.
code: theorem refl_cast {x y : X} (h : y = x) : (refl x).cast h h = refl y := by

docstring: A degenerate subpath represents the reflexivity class at its endpoint.
code:
theorem subpath_self {x y : X} (p : Path x y) (a : unitInterval) :
    mk (p.subpath a a) = refl (p a) := by

docstring: In the path-homotopy quotient, concatenating adjacent subpaths of `p` gives the larger subpath from the first endpoint to the last endpoint.
code:
theorem subpath_trans {x y : X} (p : Path x y) (a b c : unitInterval) :
    trans (mk (p.subpath a b)) (mk (p.subpath b c)) =
      mk (p.subpath a c) := by

docstring: The full `[0,1]` subpath represents the original path, up to the endpoint casts inserted by `Path.subpath`.
code:
theorem subpath_zero_one {x y : X} (p : Path x y) :
    mk (p.subpath 0 1) = (mk p).cast (by simp) (by simp) := by

docstring: The image of a based loop under a null-homotopic continuous map is null-homotopic in the target: a map homotopic to a constant collapses every loop to the constant loop.
If `γ.trans γ'.symm` is nullhomotopic, then `γ` and `γ'` are homotopic. This is the path-homotopy analogue of `a * b⁻¹ = 1 → a = b`.
code:
theorem of_trans_symm {γ γ' : Path x₀ x₁}
    (h : (γ.trans γ'.symm).Homotopic (Path.refl x₀)) : γ.Homotopic γ' :=

docstring: Left cancellation in the fundamental groupoid: if `e.trans γ` and `e.trans δ` are homotopic, then `γ` and `δ` are homotopic. This is the path-homotopy analogue of `c * a = c * b → a = b`.
code:
theorem trans_left_cancel {x₀ x₁ x₂ : X} {e : Path x₀ x₁} {γ δ : Path x₁ x₂}
    (h : (e.trans γ).Homotopic (e.trans δ)) : γ.Homotopic δ := by

docstring: Composing on the left with a null-homotopic loop does not change the homotopy class.
code:
theorem trans_left_of_nullhomotopic {γ₀ : Path x₀ x₀} {γ₁ : Path x₀ x₁}
    (hγ₀ : γ₀.Homotopic (Path.refl x₀)) : (γ₀.trans γ₁).Homotopic γ₁ :=

docstring: Right cancellation in the fundamental groupoid: if `γ.trans e` and `δ.trans e` are homotopic, then `γ` and `δ` are homotopic. This is the path-homotopy analogue of `a * c = b * c → a = b`.
code:
theorem trans_right_cancel {x₀ x₁ x₂ : X} {γ δ : Path x₀ x₁} {e : Path x₁ x₂}
    (h : (γ.trans e).Homotopic (δ.trans e)) : γ.Homotopic δ := by

docstring: Composing on the right with a null-homotopic loop does not change the homotopy class.
code:
theorem trans_right_of_nullhomotopic {γ₀ : Path x₀ x₁} {γ₁ : Path x₁ x₁}
    (hγ₁ : γ₁.Homotopic (Path.refl x₁)) : (γ₀.trans γ₁).Homotopic γ₀ :=

docstring: Restrict a path whose image lies in a subset to a path in the corresponding subtype. The source and target are the given subtype endpoints, and coercing the restricted path back to `X` recovers the original path pointwise.
The underlying point of `γ.codRestrict hmem` at time `t` is just `γ t`, viewed in `X`.
code:
theorem codRestrict_coe {s : Set X} {x y : s} (γ : Path x.val y.val)
    (hmem : ∀ t, γ t ∈ s) (t : I) :
    (γ.codRestrict hmem t : X) = γ t := by

theorem continuous_initialSegmentFamily_uncurry {a b : X} (γ : Path a b) :
    Continuous ↿(initialSegmentFamily γ) := by

docstring: The family of initial segments of `γ : Path a b`: at parameter `t : I`, the path `s ↦ γ.extend (min s t)` from `a` to `γ t` (`initialSegmentFamily_apply`). At `t = 0` this is the constant path at `a` (`initialSegmentFamily_zero`); at `t = 1` it is `γ` itself, up to a trivial right-endpoint cast (`initialSegmentFamily_one`). The property consumers actually need is joint continuity in `(t, s)`, recorded as `continuous_initialSegmentFamily_uncurry`.
code:
noncomputable def initialSegmentFamily {a b : X} (γ : Path a b) (t : I) :
    Path a (γ t) :=

@[simp] private theorem initialSegmentFamily_apply {a b : X} (γ : Path a b) (t s : I) :
    initialSegmentFamily γ t s = γ.extend (min (s : ℝ) t) := by

@[simp] theorem initialSegmentFamily_one {a b : X} (γ : Path a b) :
    initialSegmentFamily γ 1 = γ.cast rfl (by simp) := by

@[simp] theorem initialSegmentFamily_zero {a b : X} (γ : Path a b) :
    initialSegmentFamily γ 0 = (Path.refl a).cast rfl (by simp) := by

docstring: Mapping `γ.codRestrict hmem` back along the subtype inclusion recovers `γ`.
code:
theorem map_codRestrict {s : Set X} {x y : s} (γ : Path x.val y.val)
    (hmem : ∀ t, γ t ∈ s) :
    (γ.codRestrict hmem).map continuous_subtype_val = γ := by
